The official series of record is USDA Food and Nutrition Service SNAP program data; the first print used here was recovered from the ALFRED vintage archive acting strictly as a history/vintage mirror, and no official FNS release artifact was fetched for this cell.

History supplied to the forecaster, read at the ALFRED 2023-06-01 vintage and truncated at 2023-05-01: 60 monthly observations from 2016-07 to 2021-06, ending at 4,237,518 recipients. This series publishes with a multi-year lag, so at the forecast origin the newest available print was 2021-06 — 30 months before the target month. Nothing at or after the target month was available; the harness enforces the truncation.

Base rate / reference class: the trailing 60 monthly prints ending 2021-06 have mean 4,091,305 and range 3,623,654 to 4,775,267. Their 59 month-over-month changes have mean -337 and sample standard deviation 85,887 recipients per month, which is the same one-step dispersion the Brier reward export uses as its normalization scale.

Policy conditioning for this cell: `policy_context = operative_plus_purpose` — FRA 2023 §§311–314 verbatim. Provisions in the prompt: sec311_operative (sha256 e592c97a52b6); sec312_operative (sha256 e682bed8d04c); sec314_transparency (sha256 d7de1b83b56b); sec313_purpose (sha256 2f03831291fb). The statute is the Fiscal Responsibility Act of 2023, Pub. L. 118-5, Title III, enacted 2023-06-03; text is stored verbatim at `experiments/billimpact/bills/FRA-2023-118publ5.txt`.

Forecaster's own rationale, quoted verbatim from the run record (`cell_key = snap.ca.2023-12|operative_plus_purpose|point_ci_json|single_pass|claude-sonnet-5|actual|3`): "California SNAP counts had been trending near ~4.9-5.0M by mid-2023 (post-pandemic emergency allotment expiration boosting new applications and administrative backlog), and slight tightening from work-requirement changes is offset by continued elevated enrollment, so December 2023 is projected roughly flat-to-slightly-up from recent 2023 levels with moderate uncertainty due to lack of 2022-2023 data in the provided history."

Interval derivation is NOT available for this cell, and that is a property of the elicitation contract rather than an omission here: the `point_ci_json` prompt asks for a point and an 80% interval and never asks the model to disclose a sigma or a z-multiplier, so no derivation exists to publish and none is invented. Those five numbers seed the house `interval_anchor_v1` transform (`scripts/run_thesis_analyst.py:interval_distribution`) at CDF knots 0.1 / 0.5 / 0.9, and the resulting 201-point CDF is carried in `predictionDistribution`. For scale, the trailing one-step dispersion above is 85,887 per month and the target is 30 months out.

Repeat structure: this configuration was run 5 times at temperature 1.0; the emitted cell is the median-by-point repeat (rep 3), so it is an actually-elicited triple rather than a synthesised one. Across repeats the points ranged 4,950,000 to 4,950,000. That spread is the experiment's noise floor and is the object of study, not a defect.

Already-known outcome, disclosed rather than hidden: the first print for this unit is 5,318,809, discovered at ALFRED vintage 2026-02-01 with a revision of 0 to the current vintage. It was public before this experiment ran, so this cell must never enter a forward-looking scoring population.
